title: Terraform IAM module: least-privilege RBAC scaffolding for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and CI checks that scaffold IAM/RBAC resources for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments with least-privilege defaults. The module must support multi-tenant customer accounts, role separation for operator vs application workloads, permission boundaries, and automated policy testing. It should integrate with our existing IaC repo layout and be safe to run in staging and customer preview environments.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear inputs for account identifiers, environment, and role prefixes
Default roles follow least-privilege principle: operator, deployer, monitoring, read-only-admin
Permission boundaries and deny-lists configurable per environment
Module passes automated policy tests (Terraform validate + custom OPA/sentinel) in CI
Existing Private deploys can be migrated using an upgrade plan with no downtime for control-plane operations
Comprehensive docs and examples (single-tenant and multi-tenant layouts) added to repo
Security review completed and sign-off obtained
implementation_plan: Design module interface: inputs/outputs, naming conventions, and role templates (2 days)
Prototype Terraform resources for operator and workload roles with permission boundaries (3 days)
Add optional SAML/OIDC role mappings and KMS key access stubs (1 day)
Implement automated policy tests using OPA Rego rules run in CI and local pre-commit hook (2 days)
Create upgrade/migration playbook: recommended terragrunt plan steps and migration script to map old policies (2 days)
Write examples: single-tenant VPC, shared services account pattern, and customer-isolated accounts (1 day)
Run in staging preview and iterate on RBAC exceptions (ongoing)
Open PR with module, tests, docs; request security and platform reviews (1 day)
notes: We must avoid granting broad iam:PassRole or wildcard resource ARNs in defaults — require explicit opt-in via module input
Consider permission boundaries on IAM roles to prevent privilege escalation even if a role's policy is expanded later
Discussed using OPA alongside Terraform Cloud policy checks; initial CI will run Rego-based tests in GitHub Actions
KMS key access should be separate role binding with least privileges and optional trust for customer-managed keys
Migration strategy must account for existing state files and remote state locking in S3/Dynamo; include state import steps
Coordinate with Console team for expected principal names used by RBAC tooling
Potential follow-up: automated role audit job that reports unused permissions and stale role bindings
updates: 2026-02-25: Created ticket and ran a 1-hour design sync with Platform Security and Console leads. Agreed on role names and broad separation: operator, deployer, monitoring, readonly-admin.

2026-02-28: Spike completed — prototype module creates roles and attaches permission boundaries. Found that existing naming collision in terragrunt live repo requires namespace prefixing; added 'prefix' input to interface.

2026-03-03: Security requested denial of iam:CreatePolicy in defaults and recommended requiring an explicit flag to allow policy creation. Updated plan to emit managed policies only when 'allow_managed_policy' = true.
2026-03-06: Implemented OPA tests for two Rego rules: no wildcard ARNs in role policies, and no iam:PassRole on roles without explicit pass-role whitelist. CI runs these as a GitHub Actions step.
2026-03-09: Ran staging deploy with module; identified an issue where monitoring role lacked kms:Decrypt for log decryption — added optional kms_key_arn input and scoped kms statements.

2026-03-12: Draft PR opened with module, tests, and docs. Requested reviews from @jen-li (Security) and @mikael (Platform). Scheduling security review next week. Planning migration playbook and demo for infra guild meeting.
